items.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002
items.q: you hear that rhythm in groups like the Meters, who have an association with the Neville Brothers, Aaron Neville and the rest of the brothers from down there.

ctx.x: If a student was watching this interview and said a number of times you’ve mentioned the second line, they might not know what you’re talking about.

Yeah. A second line rhythm is like a rhythm from New Orleans. Now I don’t know the exact origin of it. But I think it came out of what they used to call the Cakewalk from the late nineteenth century. And it was like a dance. And so you hear the second line rhythm a lot, like if you listen to recordings of “When the Saints Go Marching In” [scats] so it’s sort of like a combination of a march and dance rhythm. And you hear that rhythm in groups like the Meters, who have an association with the Neville Brothers,…
It’s funny when I was kind of choosing a couple of things to put here I went from the Eddie Harris thing and then I put your CD on and I found some similarity there between those two songs.
